record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Resolution obstruction in the aspherical case
record.original_question: Suppose X is an aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold that has the disjoint disks property (DDP). Must X be homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold?

evidence.quote: Is every aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold having the DDP homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A space $X$ is called an absolute neighborhood retract (ANR) if it is metrizable and, whenever $X$ is embedded as a closed subset of a metric space $Y$, some neighborhood of $X$ in $Y$ retracts onto $X$. A compact ANR $X$ is called a homology ANR-manifold of dimension $n$ if for every $x \in X$ the local homology satisfies
$$H_k(X, X \setminus \{x\}; \mathbb{Z}) \cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z} & k=n,\\ 0 & k \neq n. \end{cases}$$
We say $X$ has the disjoint disks property (DDP) if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every pair of continuous maps $f, g \colon D^2 \to X$ from the 2-disk, there exist continuous maps $f', g' \colon D^2 \to X$ with $\sup d(f,f') < \varepsilon$, $\sup d(g,g') < \varepsilon$, and $f'(D^2) \cap g'(D^2) = \emptyset$. A space $X$ is called aspherical if it is path-connected and $\pi_k(X) = 0$ for all $k \geq 2$.

Question: Suppose $X$ is an aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold that has the DDP. Must $X$ be homotopy equivalent to a closed topological manifold?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold with the DDP is homotopy equivalent to a closed topological manifold appears to be open. Although compact homology ANR-manifolds with nontrivial resolution obstruction (and hence not homotopy equivalent to closed manifolds) were constructed by Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger, no aspherical example is known, and the problem is highlighted as open in surveys on aspherical manifolds and on exotic homology manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Is every aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold having the DDP homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Problems on homology manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: No example of an aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold that is not homotopy equivalent to a closed topological manifold is known.
status_evidence.claim: No aspherical counterexample is known, indicating the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Desingularizing homology manifolds (Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger)
status_evidence.snippet: Every homology n–manifold X, n ≥ 6, is the cell-like image of a DDP homology n–manifold; non-resolvable DDP homology manifolds exist.
status_evidence.claim: Constructs non-manifold DDP homology manifolds, but the aspherical case remains unresolved.
